scope: El Morro's tiered coastal fort, bastions, sentry boxes, lighthouse and principal ramps as a coordinated bounded site.

stories.title: El Morro: The Fortress That Guarded Spain's Empire

originals.caption: Courtyard of San Felipe del Morro castle, with a explanatory sign about the flags. Old San Juan, Puerto Rico
originals.inspection: 2013 full original individually inspected: ochre-yellow arcaded main parade with white arches/pilasters/cornice and green lower plinth; open-court through arch, door/window openings. Flags, people and explanatory board are not geometry.

originals.caption: Fort El Morro, San Juan, Puerto Rico, United States - Approaching the fort from the front
originals.inspection: 2009 full original individually inspected: paired low landfront bastions, deeply battered weathered walls, southeast bridge/central pedimented gate; right-hand integral blue-gray lighthouse. Lantern is temporarily scaffolded in this date; exclude scaffolding.

originals.caption: Bartizan in San Felipe del Morro castle. Old San Juan, Puerto Rico
originals.inspection: 2013 full original individually inspected: cylindrical stone garita on projecting corbel, small narrow vertical firing slit, curving pale bell-shaped cap with small ball finial and rim. No generic conical watchtower substitution.

originals.filename: Lighthouse Castillo San Felipe del Morro SJU 06 2019 6697.jpg
originals.caption: Castillo San Felipe del Morro Lighthouse, Old San Juan
originals.sourceFamily: commons:lighthouse castillo san felipe del morro sju 06 2019 6697.jpg
originals.inspection: 2019 full original individually inspected: blue-gray brick square upper lighthouse body over retained octagonal base, white corner turrets/multilayer cornice/arched window trims, dark shuttered windows, black lantern with diagonal metal glazing bars and broad curved cap/finial. Not55m tall above its own base.

originals.caption: Entrada principal al Castillo San Felipe del Morro, Viejo San Juan, Puerto Rico
originals.inspection: 2019 full original individually inspected: paired stone columns, classical triangular pediment/entablature, shallow ornament/coat-of-arms area, true round-headed sallyport passage through thick landfront wall. Unrelated signs/people and exact inscription excluded.

originals.filename: El Morro, Castillo de San Felipe.jpg
originals.caption: The highest wall of el Morro, Castillo de San Felipe, from its mid-level outdoor floor.
originals.sourceFamily: commons:el morro, castillo de san felipe.jpg
originals.inspection: 2013 full original individually inspected: high rounded/blunt Caballero battery wall, row of deeply recessed round-head windows, main steep ramp with separate stair edge, lower court and curved brick gun traverses; distinct elevation levels.

originals.caption: Photo from 5th level of El Morro looking out into the harbour.
originals.inspection: 2009-upload original individually inspected: long open sea-facing fourth battery with true splayed parapet embrasures, half-circle gun traverses, recessed lower open courts/arched entries and connecting stair/ramp; no uniform flat castle slab.

originals.filename: Castillo San Felipe del Morro from air.jpg
originals.caption: Taken from air on the way back from the island of Culebra
originals.sourceFamily: commons:castillo san felipe del morro from air.jpg
originals.inspection: 2014 aerial full original individually inspected: complete current fort massing, two landfront bastions/moat/bridge, open yellow-arcaded parade and lighthouse in right upper bastion, stepped seaward batteries and ramp courts. Esplanade/city walls/cemetery/neighboring buildings excluded.

originals.caption: Castillo San Felipe del Morro as it appeared in 2024
originals.inspection: 2024 full original individually inspected: actual multi-arch masonry entrance bridge across dry grass moat, low pedestrian parapets, central through portal and large battered front wall; six under-bridge arches visible in HABS section35. Current visitors/fixtures omitted.

referenceReview.excluded: Unrelated airport tower, streets/churches, food, wilderness, signs/interiors/people and distant city/cemetery; historical photos are comparisons only.

primarySources.inspection: Primary NPS current identity/six-level fort on high promontory, modern observation/bunker additions.140ft is promontory context, not an above-grade uniform wall/tower height.
NPS main plaza is fifth level, steep ramps reach sixth and lower levels have separate access. Qualitative level order, not measured heights.

Two-page NPS lighthouse nomination text read: current1908square brick/masonry tower around older octagonal base, lantern, corner ornamental turrets. Historical paint description differs from2019 original; modern selected photo governs finish.

NPS/HABS PR48 public measured-drawing collection index retrieved successfully through JSON API;52 contact thumbnails inspected. Selected original plans/sections locally retained by exact URL/hash. Main plan1987project/1990composite, not current cadastral survey.

NPS/HABS PR48A lighthouse five-sheet collection: all five contact thumbnails; originals2and5 inspected in detail. Square upper/octagonal base, four turrets, helical lantern bars and sections. Hidden room interiors excluded.

Archived primary NPS2025brochure PDF rendered; second page actual illustration/level diagram and site map inspected. Shows1waterbattery,2originaltower,3lowerplaza,4mainfiringbattery,5mainplaza,6landdefense. Illustrative tier order, not exact measured trace.
Linked current NPS self-guide map returns404; not evidence.
